tables.title: Crude production in Japan proper
tables.units: kiloliters, by calendar year (1 kiloliter equals 6.29 barrels or 264 U.S. gallons)
tables.period: 1942, 1943, 1945 (as printed; the third column is probably 1944) and January through August 1945
tables.totals_check: Summed each district's fields in every column: Niigata (67,534; 68,500; 66,547; 41,576), Akita (181,820; 170,401; 177,134; 103,531), Yamagata (6,324; 16,823; 17,344; 8,122) and Hokkaido (8,138; 7,007; 8,134; 4,955) all agree with the printed district totals. Grand total: summed the four district totals; 1942, 1943 and third column agree (263,816; 262,731; 269,159); Jan-Aug sum is 158,184 against printed 158,186, a disagreement of 2.
warnings: Grand total, Jan thru Aug column: printed 158,186, district totals sum to 158,184.
Third column is headed 1945 as printed, but the figures match the 1944 column of the later 'Summary of petroleum production' table, so it is probably a misprint for 1944.
Nakajo Jan thru Aug (3,684) exceeds its full-year figure (1,633), as printed.
Akita 1942 total here is 181,820; the summary table gives 181,821.
tables.ocr_check: OCR (page 67 only; page 66 was not in the OCR file) matched the Yamagata and Hokkaido rows; it rendered the blank Shonai cells as dashes, which in the image are underline rules.
tables.notes: Table runs from the bottom of PDF page 66 (printed p. 63) onto PDF page 67 (printed p. 64). Blank cells (Nakajo 1942 and 1943, Maki Jan-Aug) are blank in the original. Dashes in the Shonai row are printed as underline rules, transcribed as em dashes. District names are printed as centred headings and are kept here as rows with empty cells.

tables.title: Summary of petroleum production
tables.totals_check: Summed each year column: 1942 = 263,817, 1943 = 262,731, 1944 = 269,159, Total column = 795,707, Annual Average column = 265,236, Percent column = 100.0; all agree with the printed totals. Each row's Total (sum of three years) and Annual Average (Total/3, rounded) agree. Percentages recomputed from the totals give 25.5, 66.5, 5.1, 2.9 against printed 25.4, 66.5, 5.1, 3.0; the printed percentages themselves sum to 100.0.
warnings: Printed percentages for Niigata (25.4%) and Hokkaido (3.0%) differ by 0.1 from recomputation (25.5%, 2.9%); not corrected.
